title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 329 (Transfers not in good faith to be void)

content.overview: Any transfer of property (movable or immovable) or delivery of goods by a company, not made in the ordinary course of its business or in favour of a purchaser or encumbrancer in good faith and for valuable consideration, if made within one year before the presentation of a petition for winding up by the Tribunal or the passing of a resolution for voluntary winding up, is void against the Company Liquidator.
content.glance: Transfers or deliveries within one year that are not ordinary-course or good-faith valuable-consideration transactions are void against the liquidator.
content.study: Section 329 avoids certain pre-winding-up dispositions. The transfer or delivery must fall outside the ordinary course of the company’s business and must not be in favour of a purchaser or encumbrancer who took in good faith and for valuable consideration. The one-year look-back runs from the presentation of a Tribunal winding-up petition or from the voluntary winding-up resolution. The consequence is voidness against the Company Liquidator, enabling recovery for the estate.

sections.heading: Avoidable transfer
sections.body: Transfer of property or delivery of goods within one year before petition or voluntary resolution, not in ordinary course and not to a good-faith purchaser/encumbrancer for value, is void against the Company Liquidator.

provisions.title: Transfers not in good faith to be void

examples.title: Non-ordinary-course transfer
examples.body: Six months before a winding-up petition, the company transfers a valuable asset to a related party for a nominal sum outside the ordinary course of business. The transfer is void against the Company Liquidator under s. 329.

hypotheticals.question: Is a sale to an arm’s-length buyer for market value within the one-year window void?
hypotheticals.analysis: No, if the sale is in the ordinary course of business or the buyer is a purchaser in good faith and for valuable consideration; s. 329 does not avoid such transfers.

misconceptions.trap: Every transfer within one year is automatically void.
misconceptions.correction: Only those not in the ordinary course and not to a good-faith purchaser or encumbrancer for valuable consideration are void against the liquidator.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 329 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the transfer/delivery and the one-year window. II. Test ordinary course and good-faith valuable consideration. III. Conclude voidness against the liquidator if the exceptions fail.

examTips: State the one-year look-back and the two safe harbours (ordinary course; good-faith purchaser/encumbrancer for value).
revisionPoints: One-year void transfers not in good faith / ordinary course
